name: market-monitor
description: Watch one page and speak up ONLY when it changed in a way that matters to you — quiet by default, every alert quoting the page it came from. The host must be on your egress allow-list before the first run.

url.help: The page to watch. Its host must already be listed under Settings → Security → Allowed Egress Hosts — automated fetches use an EXCLUSIVE allow-list, so an unlisted host is refused before any request leaves the machine.

watching_for.help: What a material change looks like to you — "the pricing table", "the incident status", "the published version number". Also the stored item's identity, so repeat runs update one record instead of piling up.

max_chars.help: How much of the page to read. This can only NARROW the fetch provider's own 20,000-character ceiling — asking for more gets you the ceiling, never more than it.

metadata.why_cheap: A quiet check is one fast-tier read of the page and nothing else — the grounding judge, the write and the alert all live behind the branch, so a page that did not change costs a single cheap call.
metadata.egress_is_the_consent_surface: `net-fetch` reaches nothing until this page's host sits in `security.egress.allow_hosts`. With an empty list the first run FAILS by design, naming the host and the exact setting — that refusal is how the user grants the reach, not a defect to route around, and this template has no way to widen it.
metadata.why_quiet_by_default: An alert about a re-rendered ad slot or a bumped timestamp is how a user learns to ignore the next one. So the assessment answers one question — is this worth interrupting someone for — and the default answer is no.

steering_examples.description: Watch our provider's status page and tell me only if the incident state changes — I do not care about the maintenance calendar.
You are alerting on the copyright year in the footer — that is not a material change, ignore anything outside the pricing table.

example_outputs: one alert naming what changed and quoting the page, plus one stored record you can search later — or nothing at all
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for reading a page once — use dual-sink-watcher or paper-ingest; and not for a host you have not allow-listed, because the fetch is refused rather than attempted

children.label: What did we tell the user last time?
Read the page through the egress guard
